### Motivation

- Implement richer research-note upload flow that supports multiple files and automatically splits multi-page PDFs into per-page files on the backend for easier viewing and printing. 
- Improve the frontend research-note workspace and project-level upload UX with drag-and-drop, metadata inputs, and a simplified viewer to match the new backend behaviour. 
- Remove legacy template wiring and move server template lookup to the React app's legacy sources while slimming legacy route fallbacks. 
- Harden client-side role/session storage and session fallbacks to work in browsers with restricted storage.

### Description

- Backend: replaced single-file upload with multi-file handling in `project_upload_research_note_api` (`server/domains/projects/api.py`) to accept multiple `research_note_file` items, validate extensions, split PDFs into per-page PDF files using `PdfReader/PdfWriter`, save files under a per-note folder, update `ResearchNote.files`, and return `created_files` and `note_id` in the JSON response. 
- Frontend: added drag-and-drop and metadata fields for project uploads and multi-file uploader with file type validation, upload progress and navigation to the created PDF viewer in `apps/web/src/pages/UserGenericPages.jsx` (ProjectResearchNotesPage and ResearchNoteWorkspace changes), added A4/print styles in `apps/web/src/styles.css`, and updated routes in `apps/web/src/App.jsx`. 
- Auth & Storage robustness: introduced `hasAuthSession()` and resilient role storage with an in-memory fallback and safe access to `localStorage`/`sessionStorage` in `apps/web/src/utils/auth.js` and `apps/web/src/utils/projectContext.js`; adjusted route guards in `RouteGuards.jsx` to allow server session fallback. 
- Cleanup & config: removed many legacy client templates and references from the compiled template sources and `routeCatalog`, updated `server/config/settings.py` template `DIRS` to point at the new `apps/web/src/legacy/client` location, and removed the dynamic legacy-route rendering in `App.jsx`. 
- Tests: added `test_project_research_note_upload_splits_pdf_pages` to `server/tests/test_api.py` which creates a multi-page PDF in-memory, posts to `/api/v1/projects/{id}/research-notes/upload`, and asserts that the backend created two per-page PDF `ResearchNoteFile` records and returned `created_files == 2`.

### Testing

- Ran the Django server test suite with `pytest` (server tests); all tests completed successfully and the new test `test_project_research_note_upload_splits_pdf_pages` passed. 
- Exercised the upload endpoint `/api/v1/projects/{project_id}/research-notes/upload` in tests to verify multi-page PDF splitting and `created_files` reporting. 
- Verified frontend build changes compile locally and basic client flows for project note upload and viewer navigation in development (no failing automated frontend tests included).

## Enforce least-privilege permissions

This PR adds explicit `permissions` blocks to GitHub Actions workflow files that currently have no permissions defined, following the principle of least privilege.

### Changes
- `build.yml`: permissions: {} (defense-in-depth)

### Why
Without explicit permissions, workflows inherit the default token permissions configured at the repository or organization level. By explicitly declaring the minimum required permissions, we reduce the blast radius if a workflow is compromised.

### References
- [GitHub Actions security hardening](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions)
- [Automatic token authentication permissions](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/automatic-token-authentication#permissions-for-the-github_token)

body:
## Summary

  This PR implements the namespace and table lifecycle gaps in the Iceberg REST mock catalog and expands integration coverage for rename/delete flows.

  ## What’s implemented

  ### Namespace lifecycle

  - Added DELETE /v1/namespaces/{ns}
      - Returns 409 when namespace is non-empty or has child namespaces.
  - Added namespace properties update endpoint:
      - POST /v1/namespaces/{ns}/properties
      - Supports updates and removals with response fields updated, removed, missing.
  - Added nested namespace support:
      - Namespace creation from array parts (e.g. ["analytics","sales"] -> analytics.sales)
      - Parent-filtered listing: GET /v1/namespaces?parent=analytics

  ### Table lifecycle

  - Added DELETE /v1/namespaces/{ns}/tables/{table}.
  - Added table rename endpoint:
      - POST /v1/tables/rename
  - Added staged create semantics:
      - stage-create=true returns load response but does not persist table state.

  ### Routing and state

  - Added /v1/tables context routing so rename endpoint is reachable.
  - Extended store interfaces and implementations:
      - deleteNamespace, deleteTable, renameTable for in-memory and FDB stores.
  - Maintained Iceberg-style error envelopes (error.message/type/code) across new paths.

  ## Tests

  ### Integration harness updates

  integration/run_integration.sh now validates:

  - ALTER TABLE ... RENAME TO ...
  - read from renamed table
  - DROP SCHEMA fails when non-empty
  - DROP TABLE succeeds
  - DROP SCHEMA succeeds after table drop

  ### Unit/component tests

  Expanded HTTP tests cover:

  - nested namespace parent listing
  - namespace properties updates
  - table delete lifecycle
  - rename endpoint behavior
  - staged create non-persistence

  ## Docs

  - Updated ICEBERG_CATALOG_GAPS.md:
      - Marked sections 1 and 2 as implemented in the prototype.
      - Added TODOs for:
          - true concurrent-writer integration testing
          - FDB-mode integration parity testing

  ## Validation

  - ./gradlew test passes
  - ./integration/run_integration.sh passes with the new lifecycle checks

### Motivation

- Improve IP whitelist handling to support CIDR ranges and IPv6 for more accurate network-based allowlisting.  
- Make `DeviceHistory` persistence more robust by surfacing success/failure and only clearing dirty state on success to avoid data loss.  
- Ensure the sample app degrades gracefully when `CloudPhoneRiskAppCore` is unavailable and clarify project layout for new contributors.

### Description

- Implemented CIDR and IP parsing/matching in `RemoteConfig.WhitelistRules.contains(ip:)` with IPv4 and IPv6 support and added platform imports (`Darwin`/`Glibc`).  
- Added `ParsedIPAddress` and `ParsedCIDR` helpers to perform numeric address parsing and prefix containment checks.  
- Changed `DeviceHistory.persistToDiskLocked(resetAnchor:)` to return a `Bool` and updated `persistIfDirty()` to only clear `isDirty` when persistence succeeds.  
- Updated `DetectionViewModel.detect` to set an error state instead of providing a broken mock when `CloudPhoneRiskAppCore` is unavailable.  
- Expanded `README.md` with a project overview and SPM run instructions.  
- Added unit tests `WhitelistRulesTests` covering exact match, IPv4 CIDR, IPv6 CIDR, and invalid CIDR handling.

### Testing

- Ran `cd RiskDetectorApp && swift test` which executed the test suite including the new `WhitelistRulesTests` and completed successfully.  
- Verified that `DeviceHistory` persistence path returns `true` on success and that `isDirty` remains set when persistence fails via unit testing and local exercise of the persistence flow.  
- Confirmed the sample app falls back to an error state in non-`CloudPhoneRiskAppCore` builds via local runtime checks.

author: emerson-gray
body:
## Media Support for Thread Messages

Architecture for file attachments in thread conversations. Users attach files in the UI message composer; agents receive them as LLM content parts.

### New: `architecture/media.md`

**File lifecycle:**
1. UI uploads file via Gateway → stored in object storage → returns file reference (id, url, filename, contentType, size).
2. UI sends message with text + file IDs → Threads stores message with file references.
3. Agent reads messages → maps files to OpenAI `input_image` (images) or `input_file` (everything else) content parts with pre-signed URLs.

**Object storage:**
- S3-compatible API. MinIO for local development (bootstrap_v2), any S3 provider in production.
- Objects keyed: `<team_id>/threads/<thread_id>/<file_id>/<filename>`.
- All access via pre-signed URLs (no public bucket access).

**API changes:**
- `POST /api/threads/{threadId}/files` — new upload endpoint (multipart).
- `SendMessage` body extended: `{ text, files: [{ id }] }` — optional file references.
- `GetMessages` response extended: each file includes `{ id, filename, contentType, sizeBytes, url }` with fresh pre-signed download URLs.

**Agent integration:**
- `HumanMessage` extended to produce multi-part content arrays (text + image/file parts).
- `image/*` → `input_image` with `image_url`. All others → `input_file` with `file_url`.

**UI:**
- Composer: attachment button, upload progress, removable file chips.
- Display: inline image thumbnails, file name + size + download link for non-images.

### Updated: `architecture/threads.md`
- Message model: added `files` field.
- `SendMessage` description updated to include file references.

### Updated: `architecture/system-overview.md`
- Added Object Storage (S3) to Data Stores table.

### New open question: Context Size Measurement with Media
- Current summarization estimates tokens from `text.length / 4` — invalid for media.
- Planned direction: use `usage.input_tokens` from LLM response for actual measurement.
- Open questions: how summarization trigger works with post-call measurement, how media interacts with summarization fold, whether `summarizationKeepTokens` includes media costs.

## Enforce least-privilege permissions

This PR adds explicit `permissions` blocks to GitHub Actions workflow files that currently have no permissions defined, following the principle of least privilege.

### Changes
- `cargo.yml`: contents: read
- `image.yml`: permissions: {} (defense-in-depth)
- `nix-image.yaml`: permissions: {} (defense-in-depth)

### Why
Without explicit permissions, workflows inherit the default token permissions configured at the repository or organization level. By explicitly declaring the minimum required permissions, we reduce the blast radius if a workflow is compromised.

### References
- [GitHub Actions security hardening](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions)
- [Automatic token authentication permissions](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/automatic-token-authentication#permissions-for-the-github_token)

### Motivation
- Make Sword v1 combo behavior more consistent by treating missed swings (left-click air/block) as the action that resets combos while allowing being hit to no longer interrupt a combo. 
- Ensure a combo reset immediately terminates any active sword ultimate/autocrit state so players can't keep buffs after missing. 
- Expose tunables so autocrit damage and Trident wave movement speed can be adjusted without code changes.

### Description
- Stop resetting sword combo on incoming damage by turning `onPlayerDamage` into a no-op and instead adding `onLeftClick(Player, Action)` in `SwordAbility` to detect `LEFT_CLICK_AIR`/`LEFT_CLICK_BLOCK` as misses and call `resetComboState` to clear `combo`, `comboUltimate`, `ultimateReady` and end an active ultimate via `endUltimate` when appropriate.
